result.summary: This pull request refactors validation and blockstorage routines to return util::Result and FlushResult objects instead of silently triggering AbortNode. It allows callers to inspect error information directly, bubble up failures, and manage disk flush outcomes. The changes also expand util::Result to support arbitrary InfoType metadata and multiple error/warning message collections.
result.problem: Validation functions frequently handle fatal errors internally by invoking AbortNode and initiating shutdown, without returning failure information to callers. For libbitcoinkernel applications, catching and handling these failures is cumbersome because it requires subscribing to global notification callbacks rather than handling returned error values.

open_concerns: purpleKarrot expressed an architectural objection against util::Result style error handling in Bitcoin Core, arguing C++ exceptions or C++23 mechanisms are preferable for performance-sensitive paths
resolved_concerns: maflcko noted fragility in wrapping InterruptResult inside Result; author agreed with inverting the type representation
optout21 noted an inconsistency where FlushStateToDisk errors were ignored yet altered validation state, which was documented and split off into #35621

result.card: This PR refactors validation and block storage functions to return error information via util::Result and FlushResult rather than triggering AbortNode. This enables libbitcoinkernel embedders to detect and handle fatal validation errors programmatically rather than depending on global callbacks. It also extends util::Result with InfoType and message merging helpers. The PR is stacked on open PR 25665, has seen multiple rebases and active discussion among kernel contributors, and faces an unresolved high-level objection from purpleKarrot regarding Result-type paradigms.
